## Highlights

**coyotenote-web** has a calmer, writing-focused design, a new text style menu and several fixes that keep your edits safe. The terminal app is unchanged.

## coyotenote-web (experimental)

### A calmer place to write

- One header row and one editor bar give the note the rest of the window.
- The note list shows each note's title, edit date and opening line.
- The **text style** menu previews Normal text and Heading 1–6 in their own type. Use it by mouse or keyboard, or press **Ctrl Alt 0–6** (**⌘ ⌥ 0–6** on a Mac).
- Messages explain unsaved edits, conflicts and recovered drafts in plain terms, and dialogs are named by what they do.

### Your edits are safer

- A browser tab no longer saves into a different vault after the app restarts on another one. The tab keeps your edits for download and asks you to reload.
- Text typed while another note is loading is saved instead of disappearing from view.
- **Write** keeps notes in Markdown view when they have YAML front matter that starts with a byte order mark, TOML (`+++`) front matter or reference-style link definitions, so those are no longer rewritten. Restoring a browser draft follows the same rule.
- When a rename, trash or restore finishes but the folder change cannot be confirmed on disk, the app reports the move with a warning instead of an error. A rename in that situation still updates links to the note.

## Releases

A release is now built only from a commit on `main` that passes every check, and each release must have its notes.

## Downloads

One archive for **Linux amd64** holds `coyotenote`, `coyotenote-web`, the README, the license and third-party notices. Check it against `SHA256SUMS`. `govulncheck` and `npm audit` report no known vulnerabilities.

[Full changelog: v0.4.0 → v0.5.0](https://github.com/eg36/Coyotenote/compare/v0.4.0...v0.5.0)
